issues.where: modules/gui/macosx_redesign/module/bridge/MXRServicesBridge.m queueCommand playNow (~lines 1264-1271); engine paths src/player/player.c:1085-1123, 1228-1255, 1282 and src/player/input.c:270-274
issues.description: The C-01 fix is wrong whenever a media is already loaded, which is the common case: opening a file while another one is open or playing. vlc_player_SetStartPaused only works when vlc_player_Start creates the input synchronously. If an input already exists, vlc_playlist_PlayAt -> vlc_player_SetCurrentMedia hands the old input to the destructor and defers the new one. vlc_player_Start then sets started=true and returns (player.c:1237-1251), and the bridge immediately resets the flag with SetStartPaused(false). The destructor thread later opens the new media and calls vlc_player_input_Start directly (input.c:274), which never reads start_paused. I reproduced this with a probe that runs the bridge's exact sequence (Insert, Remove old, SetStartPaused(true), PlayAt, SetStartPaused(false)) against the real engine and the test media (probe/startpaused.c and startpaused.out under the verify-r1 directory). Case A, open paused with nothing loaded: PAUSED (correct). Case C, open paused while another file is PLAYING: PLAYING at 1.89 s. So 'Start playing when opened' off (SET-02) no longer works when replacing current media. The old per-item ':start-paused' handled this case and only leaked to items 2..N. QueueStartPausedTests checks only the Swift wire argument, so it cannot catch this. Suggested root-cause fix: add 'start-paused' only to inputs[index] with input_item_AddOption, since input.c:656 var_InheritBool reads item options. Then clear it after start: a one-shot flag consumed in on_current_media_changed/on_state_changed for that item, or remove it from the item once it reaches PAUSED. Alternatively, keep a bridge-side one-shot 'pause when this item first reaches PLAYING'. Add a native runtime test for the 'replace while playing' case.

C-02's 'select the existing sidecar' path compares MD5(url) as given by Swift with the ES str-id prefix, which is MD5 of the MRL VLC built with vlc_path2uri. vlc_path2uri percent-encodes sub-delims, while Swift's URL.absoluteString leaves them as they are. Verified: Swift gives file:///m/Movie%20(2020)%20Director's%20Cut.srt, while VLC encodes ( ) ' as %28 %29 %27. For any sidecar named like 'Movie (2020).srt', dropping or adding it again therefore does not select the existing track: the file is loaded a second time and a duplicate subtitle track appears. Fix: canonicalise before hashing (vlc_uri2path, then vlc_path2uri for file URLs) on both the lookup and the _addedTrackURLs keys. The fix is correct for plain names such as the test media.

C-10 asked to delete the snapshot-equality shortcut. It was moved to Swift instead: 'guard filters != current' compares with decodedVideoEffects, which changes only when the coalesced effects topic arrives. If a value is changed and then changed back before that snapshot arrives (slider drag, quick toggle), the last call equals the stale snapshot and is dropped, so the engine keeps the intermediate value. This is less fragile than the old NSDictionary compare, but it is still an equality gate against lagging state. Remove the guard, or compare with the last value sent instead. The resolution path (settings set+save, MXRTopicEffects on preferred-resolution) is correct, and its test passes.

C-05 is implemented and the native 'extensions' suite passes for both runtime tests (I re-ran them). Two remaining risks. (1) Trigger-only scripts run extension_Trigger synchronously on the serial service queue, so a slow trigger stalls every extension/renderer request, and the dispatch_sync in finishShutdown waits for it at quit. (2) extension_SetInput is called under manager->lock and takes the extension's running_lock (modules/lua/extension.c:530), so a long-running Lua command, such as a VLsub download, blocks the service queue. Qt uses the same pattern, so this is acceptable, but nothing measures it. Not a correctness failure.

C-03: the mode check in MXROutputOptions is correct and is covered by contracts. The auxiliary-vout tagging walks the window's parents to find the variable set on the output player, which relies on the sout display vout's parent chain (display.c resource parent -> stream -> ... -> input -> player). It also casts the opaque vlc_player_t to vlc_object_t. No native or runtime test checks that a 'Play locally while streaming' vout is actually tagged auxiliary and does not take the main surface, so this part is plausible but unverified.

Stale documentation after C-05. D045 still says 'the shipping bridge reports no extension-dialog provider ... Implementing the Lua extension-dialog provider is the real fix and is tracked separately', and the SettingsExtensionsView comment says the same. Both belong to F-settings/the integrator, not C-bridge. D039 itself was updated correctly.

Not fixed; handed to the owner with corrected evidence. The fixer corrected the false D039 claim ('bridge cannot implement'): caopengllayer has libplacebo GL tone mapping, and avsamplebuffer (the default) has no override, so Off would mean giving up PiP/EDR. That is an acceptable deferral for a minor item, but the HDR selector still offers only Auto, so the Figma Auto/Off/... list is not reached.

The services now join in parallel with signposts. The services are independent: each owns its own queue, preparser and playlist, so I see no new shared-state race. Quit latency is still not measured on the installed app. The Mac became idle, but the native lock was held by B-controls and then J-media-io for longer than I could wait, so I cancelled the live run without acquiring the lock or launching the app.

summary:
Not passing. One major regression remains: the C-01 fix makes 'Open paused' fail whenever another media is already loaded. The rest of the claimed fixes check out in code and tests, with minor gaps.

How I checked: `swift build` passes. `swift test --filter MXRVLCBackendTests` passes (54 tests), and so do the OpenAutoplay, MediaSource, LibrarySourceBrowser and Extension filters. I re-ran `native-tests.py --suite extensions` and both runtime tests pass (a real Lua dialog is drawn, typed text and a click reach the script, quit does not wait for main). No engine files changed. My outputs are under scratchpad/final/C-bridge-verify-r1/.

**C-01 (major, reproduced):** `vlc_player_SetStartPaused` only applies when `vlc_player_Start` creates the input on the spot. When an input already exists, the player defers the new media to its destructor thread. That thread later calls `vlc_player_input_Start` directly (input.c:274), which never reads start_paused, and by then the bridge has already reset the flag. My probe (probe/startpaused.c, startpaused.out) runs the bridge's exact sequence against the real engine and test media:
- Open paused with nothing loaded: PAUSED (correct).
- Open paused while another file is playing: PLAYING at 1.89 s (wrong).

So 'Start playing when opened' off (SET-02) breaks in the most common case. The old per-item option did not have this bug. The Swift-only QueueStartPausedTests cannot catch it.

**Verified as correct:**
- C-03: mode check in the output options.
- C-05: dialog provider, activation, trigger and menu work.
- C-06: mouse routing is synchronous; the filter flag is updated by a variable callback.
- C-07: shortcuts reload once per coalesced topic.
- C-08: the silent service filter is removed.
- C-11: audio devices come from the engine's list.
- C-12: repeat/random are persisted in the listener callbacks.
- C-13: services are joined in parallel.
- C-14: discovery is no longer started by reads.

**Minor gaps:**
- C-02: the 'select the existing sidecar' path fails for file names with characters like parentheses or apostrophes. Swift and VLC encode those differently, so the hashes don't match and the file loads a second time as a duplicate track.
- C-10: the equality shortcut was moved to Swift, not deleted. It compares against a lagging snapshot and can drop a change that returns to the previous value before the snapshot arrives.
- C-05: trigger-only extensions run synchronously on the service queue.
- C-03: no test checks that a stream's local video copy is tagged auxiliary and stays off the main surface.
- D045 and the SettingsExtensionsView comment still say there is no extension-dialog provider (F-settings' files).
- C-09: HDR 'Off' is deferred to the owner, with corrected reasoning in D039.
- C-13: quit latency is still not measured in the real app. The Mac became idle, but other agents held the native lock too long, so I cancelled the live run without taking the lock or launching the app.
